questions.q: What is a predominant feature of entrepreneurial activity?
options: Studying emerging technologies
Identifying opportunities and risk taking
Designing the manufacturing system of the product
Conducting a suitable marketing campaign and a life-cycle assessment
questions.explanation: Entrepreneurial activity is defined by spotting market opportunities and being willing to take calculated risks to exploit them. The other options are specific design or production tasks, not the defining characteristic of entrepreneurship.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of developing scale models for projects?
options: To demonstrate the method of construction
To demonstrate the aesthetic aspects of the project
To ensure working drawings of the project are correct
To provide an effective means of communicating the project ideas to others
questions.explanation: A scale model is primarily a communication tool — it presents the design concept in three dimensions so others can understand and respond to the ideas. The other options are partial benefits but not the main purpose of modelling.

questions.q: Which of the following is the most important consideration for designers when selecting a technique to demonstrate a client's design brief?
options: Making ideas persuasive for the intended audience
Cost of the presentation and prototype development
Making ideas easily understood by the intended audience
Creating an 'eye-catching' presentation for the intended audience
questions.explanation: The core purpose of communicating a design brief is clarity, so the technique chosen must make the ideas easily understood by the intended audience. Persuasion, cost and visual appeal are secondary to the message being clearly conveyed.

questions.q: In a design brief for a product, system or environment, what is the main purpose of the design specifications provided by a client to a designer?
options: They summarise all features used in the design.
They outline aspects of the design in order to meet specific needs.
They examine market trends, legal requirements and budget figures.
They list important social and environmental considerations in the design.
questions.explanation: Design specifications set out the requirements the design must satisfy, outlining the aspects needed to meet the client's specific needs. They guide and constrain the solution rather than summarising features or analysing markets.

questions.q: Successful completion of a major design project depends on a student making the correct link between
options: action and time management.
sustainability and appropriateness of materials.
experimentation and development of practical skills.
generation of concept designs and organising materials.
questions.explanation: Completing a major project on time relies on linking the action plan to the time plan so tasks are sequenced and scheduled realistically. The other pairings are useful but do not directly determine whether the whole project is completed.

questions.q: Terry is asked to design a product that will be accessible to a range of different cultures. Which of the following would be a major consideration for Terry?
options: Targeting the needs of people
Identifying separate market segments
Using local employees during production
Developing a product that is suitable for all market segments
questions.explanation: To make a product accessible across many cultures, the designer must develop something suitable for all market segments rather than targeting one group. This inclusive approach addresses the diverse cultural needs stated in the brief.

questions.q: Which of the following factors has the most significant effect on the success of a marketing plan?
options: The cost of the product
Use of television and radio
Understanding the market segment
Effective packaging and the point of sale
questions.explanation: A marketing plan succeeds when it is built on a clear understanding of the target market segment, because that knowledge shapes pricing, advertising and packaging decisions. The other factors are tactics that only work once the segment is understood.

questions.q: What effect does obsolescence have on the development of products?
options: It encourages the use of new technologies.
It ensures the production of sustainable products.
It limits the number of products and spare parts sold.
It creates a market for the sale of second-hand products and parts.
questions.explanation: Obsolescence drives designers to incorporate new technologies so products are continually superseded and replaced. It works against sustainability and tends to increase, not limit, the volume of new products sold.

questions.q: A designer has been commissioned to design a new hot-drink dispensing system and needs to identify suitable materials for the cups. What is the best course of action for evaluating the most suitable materials for these cups?
options: Make a working model and test the operation of the system.
Invite a focus group to evaluate the range of materials that have been selected.
Investigate the properties of possible materials and trial them in similar situations.
Seek expert advice on the range of materials available and use those that have been recommended.
questions.explanation: The most reliable evaluation comes from investigating the properties of candidate materials and testing them under conditions similar to actual use. This evidence-based trialling gives objective data, unlike opinion-based focus groups or recommendations alone.

questions.q: A graph shows information about four products (A, B, C and D) that are similar in design and production. For each product the graph compares volume of sales, profit on sales, volume of material used, and product returns. Which product is likely to have the greatest positive impact in terms of its social responsibility?
options: A
B
C
D
questions.explanation: Social responsibility is greatest for the product that uses the least material and generates the fewest returns while still achieving strong sales, minimising resource use and waste. The graph identifies product C as best meeting this balance.

questions.q: Describe how the changing nature of communication technologies has affected teamwork and collaborative design processes.

criteria.descriptor: Provides characteristics and features of the changing nature of communication technologies and the effects this has had on teamwork and collaborative design processes
Sketches in general terms how teamwork and/or collaborative design processes have been affected due to the changing nature of communication technologies

questions.q: What role does aesthetics play in influencing consumer purchasing decisions?

criteria.descriptor: Makes the relationship evident between aesthetic factors and consumer purchasing decisions, through cause and effect statements
Provides characteristics and features of the relationship between aesthetic factors and consumer purchasing decisions, using examples
Identifies an aesthetic factor OR consumer purchasing decisions

questions.q: Describe how designers may utilise new technologies when evaluating and marketing their processes and products.

criteria.descriptor: Provides the characteristics and features of how designers utilise new technologies in BOTH evaluating and marketing processes and products
Provides characteristics and features of how designers utilise new technologies in evaluating and/or marketing processes and products
Sketches in general terms how designers utilise new technologies with a reference to evaluating and/or marketing processes and products
Identifies a way designers utilise technology

questions.q: Explain the technological changes that may result from the integration of emerging technologies into new products or systems.

criteria.descriptor: Makes the relationship evident between technological changes and the possible integration of emerging technologies. Cites specific examples of cause and effect.
Discusses or provides advantages and disadvantages of possible technological changes with direct reference to the integration of emerging technologies
Provides characteristics and features of a possible technological change with reference to the integration of an emerging technology
Identifies an emerging technology or a possible technical change

questions.q: Analyse the social and economic impacts of these new products or systems.

criteria.descriptor: Draws out and relates implications of both social and economic impacts in relation to these new products or systems
Provides reasons why and/or how these new products or systems impact upon society and the economy
Identifies issues and provides evidence of the social and economic impact of these new products or systems
Provides characteristics and features of social and/or economic impacts of these new products or systems
Sketches in general terms a social or economic impact of these new products or systems
Identifies a social and/or economic impact of these new products or systems
